messages.author: cfaa93bc8692cf13
messages.subject: Trouble with data import
parts:
hi, 

I'm new to spatial analysis, and have been mapping my data using the tmap and ggplot2 packages (successfully importing, projecting and plotting my data). However, when I try to extend into the ctmm, I'm having problems even importing my data correctly.
 
Here is my code; (just for one animal at the moment - I dropped the extra variables to see if this was causing any issues). NB ALLmales is a data frame that I've successfully converted to a spatial data frame for other packages.

GRG <- filter(ALLmales, collarid == "Garango")
GRG <- subset(GRG, select = -c(HDOP, SPEED, HEADING, HACCURACY,TIMETOFIX, RETRIES))
GRG<- rename(GRG, timestamp = DATETIME)
GRG <- rename(GRG, ID = collarid)
GRG <- as.telemetry(GRG, timezone = "UTC+03", timeformat = "auto", projection =
                            "longlat +ellps=WGS84 +datum=WGS84 +no_defs")

> head(GRG)
# A tibble: 6 × 4
  ID      timestamp                  LATITUDE LONGITUDE
  <chr>   <dttm>                        <dbl>     <dbl>
1 Garango 2019-07-25 00:11:23.000000    -2.68      37.3
2 Garango 2019-07-25 01:11:19.000000    -2.68      37.3
3 Garango 2019-07-25 02:11:36.000000    -2.68      37.3
4 Garango 2019-07-25 03:00:10.000000    -2.68      37.3
5 Garango 2019-07-25 04:00:12.000000    -2.68      37.3
6 Garango 2019-07-25 05:00:36.000000    -2.68      37.3

But I get error messages as follows;

Minimum sampling interval of 0 microseconds in Garango
Error in sp::CRS(proj) : NA
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In telemetry.clean(telist[[i]], id = id[i]) :
  Times might be out of order or duplicated in Garango. Make sure that timeformat and timezone are correctly specified.
2: In telemetry.clean(telist[[i]], id = id[i]) :
  Duplicate times in Garango. Data cannot be fit without an error model.

I'm confused because AnyDuplicated(GRG) returns a 0, and the timestamp is a recognised POSIXct object. However for this animal I have two different collar manufacturers and I have written code to merge the datasets. I'm wondering
(1) how I set my timezone correctly
(2) if there's a problem with my date time format 
(3) what else I'm missing

Any help would be much appreciated  - I'm working on a poster for a conference next week.  

Many thanks!

Vicki

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: Trouble with data import
parts:
Hi Vicki,

To me it looks like your timestamp column is already stored as a POSIXct and not a character value, so the timeformat and timezone arguments are going to be ignored as there is no character -> POSIXct conversion to do on import. I would make sure the timestamps are correct before as.telemetry().

Does it import without error if you remove the projection argument? ctmm requires a locally flat projection in meters, which that argument does not provide.

If that doesn't fix the issue, then please message me with some data and I can take a look.

Best,
Chris
